title: Refute Printed.sLocalStandardThetaTensor_factorization (Ch06 Sec2_Printed, Theorem 6.2.2.1(1), pp. 299–301)
body:
Closes #4867

Refutes `Printed.sLocalStandardThetaTensor_factorization` (Theorem 6.2.2.1(1), (6.2.2.7)–(6.2.2.10), pp. 299–301) in `RiemannMasullo/Ch06_LocalGlobal/Sec2_Printed.lean`. Only the proof of `Printed.sLocalStandardThetaTensor_factorization_false` and private helpers above it were added, plus four imports (`ForMathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`, `ForMathlib.NumberTheory.NumberField.Completion.FinitePlace`, `ForMathlib.Analysis.Distribution.SchwartzSpace.Gaussian`, Mathlib's `NumberField.ClassNumber` and `Padics.HeightOneSpectrum`).

**Counterexample.** F = ℚ, S = {v} with v the prime 2 (q = N(v) = 2), ω = 1, χ = 1, r = the constant family 1, x = 1.
- Archimedean test f(t) = (q² − t²)·exp(−t²) (a Schwartz function, even, nonzero at ±1, zero at ±q).
- Finite test at v: the indicator of {z : ‖z‖ = q⁻¹} (locally constant, compact support, zero at 0).
- Left side: for every norm-one S-idele g, y = g⁻¹ satisfies ‖y_∞‖·‖y_v‖ = 1, so wherever the finite factor is nonzero, ‖y_∞‖ = q and f vanishes. The integrand is identically 0.
- Right side: the archimedean average is ∑_k ∫_{N∞} f(a⁻¹) = (q² − 1)e⁻¹ · ν(N∞), and N∞ = {±1} is finite, so its Haar mass is finite and positive. The finite factor is μ{g : ‖g‖ = q}, which is the mass of the integer units (translate by a uniformizer), i.e. the different mass, finite and positive. So the right side is nonzero.

The hypotheses used: Pic of the S-integers of ℚ is trivial (a localization of the PID 𝓞 ℚ, via `picMapAlgebra_surjective_of_isLocalization`); ω = 1 is unramified outside S and its descent is 1 (by uniqueness in `normOneCharacterUnramifiedOutside_iff`); `classNumber ℚ = 1` gives the class representatives.

The witnesses differ slightly from the docstring (which uses a compactly supported bump and the indicator of pℤₚˣ): here the archimedean test is (q² − t²)e^{−t²} and the finite test is the indicator of the sphere of radius q⁻¹, which is the same set.
